source_text: The patient is a 44-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis admitted with chest pain. MI has been ruled out. REST ECHO: EF 60%. No wall motion abnormalities. EKG shows normal sinus rhythm with mild ST depressions. The patient exercised for 7 minutes 30 seconds on a standard Bruce protocol, exceeding target heart rate; no angina nor significant ECG changes seen. Peak stress echo imaging shows EF of 75%, no regional wall motion abnormalities. Resting systolic blood pressure was approximately 152 mmHg with appropriate response to exercise. No dysrhythmias were noted. IMPRESSION: Negative exercise ECG/echocardiogram stress evaluation for inducible ischemia in excess of target heart rate. Resting hypertension with appropriate response of blood pressure to exercise. There were no complications of the procedure.
